transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Price, Maya Chen / Ravi Patel, Clara Nguyen, Alicia Morales

Auto-summary: Quick sync to review proposal consolidation, region activation timeline, and outstanding legal/billing asks.
Topics: see topics list.

[00:00] Jordan Price: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um we'll keep this tight, 30, 40 minutes ish. Jordan from Redwood, with Maya our SE.
[00:12] Ravi Patel: yep, thanks, appreciate it. Alicia and Clara here as well. Quick note, we're on a tight PO cadence this month.
[00:22] Jordan Price: understood. main goals today — one, confirm commitment consolidation across our three contracts; two, lock eu/apac activation dates; three, go over any KMS/VPC gating items.
[00:35] Clara Nguyen: can you also run through the billing cadence? last time there was some confusion about monthly vs quarterly invoices.
[00:43] Jordan Price: absolutely. We'll put options in the spreadsheet — monthly invoicing or net-30 quarterly, whichever fits procurement.

[01:05] Maya Chen: quick SE note before we get into pricing — we ran a quick internal baseline with your sample-ish prompts; aggregated latency for Redwood Dedicated in eu-west-1 was about 42ms p50 for 1k token payload, p95 around 160ms. Hosted fallback bumped p95 to ~250ms on cold prefix. but there is warm-KV cache improvement.
[01:30] Ravi Patel: interesting. those p95 numbers are... acceptable for most of our user flows but the trading alerts path needs p95 < 120ms.
[01:40] Maya Chen: understood, for the alerts flow we suggest pinning to a lower-seq-model variant and prioritizing on-dedicated pool. Also continuous batching configs can be tuned.

[02:05] Speaker 1: (mumbled) do you mean the kv cash —
[02:08] Maya Chen: yes, K-V cache, sorry transcription picked that up weirdly — the KV cache warm path cuts token generation cost and latency if your prefixes are reused.

[03:00] Jordan Price: on commitments — silverquill currently has three active small commits across teams. We recommend consolidation into a single committed pool to unlock a steeper discount and simpler routing.
[03:22] Alicia Morales: consolidation is appealing but procurement needs clear granularity on how overage billing will work and a monthly cap. we can't have surprise overages.
[03:34] Jordan Price: we'll include a hard cap option and pre-notice alerts at 70/85/95% with an automatic burst purchase path — bursts bill at the agreed burst rate in the spreadsheet.

[04:10] Clara Nguyen: what about region activation? we need eu-west-1 by April 15 and ap-southeast-1 by May 1. are those dates realistic?
[04:22] Maya Chen: yes, from an infra side eu-west-1 can be staged by April 12 for Dedicated, assuming we get the consolidated commit and capacity reservation this week. ap-southeast often needs a slightly longer lead for GPU scheduling, May 1 is tight but doable if we accept a small buffer window.
[04:45] Ravi Patel: we also have strict data residency and KMS controls in EU — key wrapping must be customer-managed.
[04:54] Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integration; for Dedicated in a managed VPC we can stitch your KMS using our connector, or for Private deployment we hand over the control plane. there's a short checklist.

[06:00] Jordan Price: legal redlines? Alicia?
[06:05] Alicia Morales: main asks: 1) monthly invoices option; 2) right to audit logs (we need 12 months retention); 3) SOC2 report or ISO statement; 4) clearer SLAs for latency-sensitive endpoints.
[06:22] Jordan Price: we can provide SOC2 letter and audit logs exports. SLA for latency is trickier — we do uptime SLAs and per-route latency monitoring, but hard p95 guarantees require Dedicated with pinned pool. we'll note that in the proposal.

[07:10] Maya Chen: to add, for the latency sensitive route we recommend a canary policy: route 100% of alerts to dedicated pool, route non-critical traffic to hosted with automatic fallback. that keeps cost lower while guaranteeing SLO for alerts.
[07:30] Ravi Patel: yeah that sounds fine. what's the expected unit cost delta if we do that split?
[07:37] Jordan Price: rough thumb — dedicated committed unit cost is ~30-40% cheaper for steady state token volume; hosted fallback is higher but only used as spill. Final numbers will be in the sheet.

[08:15] Speaker 2: (inaudible)
[08:20] Maya Chen: on perf testing — we'll need your anonymized prompt set, ideally 1-2k examples that represent alerts vs normal chat so we can run targeted 30k token/day tests across regions. Ravi, can you provide that?
[08:32] Ravi Patel: yes, I can scrub and share by Monday. will it be enough to validate p95 targets?
[08:39] Maya Chen: yes, especially if we include sequence length distribution and concurrency profile. we'll also show KV cache benefits by including repeated prefixes.

[09:50] Jordan Price: billing specifics — Alicia, would monthly invoicing with PO be acceptable if we include a consolidated commit and a monthly cap?
[10:00] Alicia Morales: that should work. we need vendor legal to confirm but monthly is preferred. Also need clear line items for Dedicated vs Hosted fallback usage.

[11:10] Clara Nguyen: on the network side, VPC peering — do you require a dedicated NAT or can we use our transit gateway?
[11:20] Maya Chen: transit gateway is fine; we support transit and SD-WAN setups. we'll provide network diagrams for your infra team.

[12:05] Jordan Price: ok recapping, action items we'll capture: Jordan to update pricing, Maya to run perf tests, Ravi to share prompts, Alicia to confirm PO window. Any other blockers?
[12:20] Ravi Patel: just one — will consolidation affect existing entitlements for our internal dev team sandboxes? some teams use small commit pools for dev.
[12:30] Jordan Price: yes you can carve dev pools as sub-allocations in the consolidated commit; we'll show allocation examples in the spreadsheet.

[13:05] Speaker 3: (brief)
[13:10] Maya Chen: also related to custodial keys — if you go Private we hand over KMS entirely; for dedicated we do connector-based CMK wrapping, both satisfy your residency ask.
[13:25] Alicia Morales: good, we prefer the connector route first. Private is heavier from a legal and ops perspective.

[15:00] Jordan Price: timeline proposal — we aim to send the consolidated pricing by Tuesday (2/16), perf results by Thursday (2/18), and alignment call for signature readiness w/c 2/22. is that workable?
[15:12] Ravi Patel: yes. Alicia will need one week to run procurement.
[15:18] Alicia Morales: that's fine. we'll aim PO for first week of March.

[16:00] Speaker 1: small question on burst lanes — if we auto-burst do you reserve capacity immediately or queue?
[16:10] Maya Chen: bursts are soft-allocated when capacity available; if underlying region is saturated we fall back to hosted fallback or route to alternate region per routing policy. we can add a strict fallback to prevent any routing to other regions for compliance reasons.
[16:30] Clara Nguyen: can we limit fallback to only warm-cached prefixes?
[16:35] Maya Chen: yes, routing rules are configurable per route; we'll outline options.

[18:00] Jordan Price: okay, any final legal or security items?
[18:06] Alicia Morales: just want the SOC2 attestation and 12-month audit log retention in writing.
[18:12] Jordan Price: we'll include both in the commitment doc.

[20:00] Maya Chen: last technical note — if you care about p95 under 120ms for alerts, Dedicated with pinned pool + KV-cache warm path is the recommended architecture. we can also supply small ML model variants to reduce seq length.
[20:20] Ravi Patel: thanks. do you have a quick sketch of cost delta for that architecture?
[20:25] Jordan Price: yep will be in the updated sheet; expect dedicated to be cheaper per token but with reserved monthly commit.

[22:00] Jordan Price: great, we'll send the updated materials and propose a signature readiness check on Feb 23.
[22:10] Ravi Patel: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[22:25] Clara Nguyen: thanks.
[22:30] Alicia Morales: thanks all.

End recap:
- Jordan to share updated consolidated commitment proposal (includes monthly invoicing option, hard caps, tiered discounts) — due 2027-02-16.
- Maya to run regional perf tests and share CSV/readout — due 2027-02-18.
- Ravi to provide anonymized prompt set and latency targets — due 2027-02-15.
- Alicia to confirm procurement timeline and PO window — due 2027-02-20.

Notes on transcription: speaker labels occasionally generic; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "KV cache" as "K-V cash").
